decisions.title: What durable trace does a killed seat leave on the board?
decisions.body: Today the lane writes an error-phase status entry and the page uses it only to stop the composing animation. The human needs to see, after the fact, that the turn died, on which seat, and why. Which carrier?

options.text: Render the existing error-phase status entry as a notice in the notification lane, homed on the channel, with the tier and the reason in its text.
pcr: Buys: no new log kind; the entry already exists on every failure path, so nothing is dropped between the lane and the page.
Costs: the page's projector has to learn to home a status entry as a notice, and the notice text is whatever the lane stringified from the exception.
Forces: every error-phase status becomes visible, including ones the page today deliberately ignores, if any exist.

options.text: Route an unreachable seat through the same '_lost' informational path a refused expert reply takes, so it lands as an informational on the channel.
pcr: Buys: one failure vocabulary on the board; the human already knows what a lost informational looks like.
Costs: the '_lost' path is shaped around a document the appender refused; an unreachable seat has no document, so the path needs a second entry point.
Forces: the informational is homed on nodes by the projector's rules, and a ruling turn with no node may have nowhere to land.

options.text: A new log kind, 'seat-failure', with its own projector rule and its own board rendering.
pcr: Buys: an exact shape for the case, with the tier, the reason, the elapsed time and the turn it interrupted.
Costs: a schema addition, a projector rule, a page rendering, and tests for each; the largest diff of the three.
Forces: the fold and the capture both learn a new kind.

decisions.title: How does the obligation the dead turn carried survive?
decisions.body: The turn that died was owed a ruling on the decisions the human's answer put in question. The escalation module recomputes the channel's resting obligation from the log on the next turn, rather than storing it. Is that enough, or does the failure need to re-arm something?

options.text: Nothing stored: the next turn on the channel recomputes the obligation from the log, so the trace from d1 only needs to tell the human to send another turn.
pcr: Buys: zero new state; correct by construction if the recomputation really does see the unresolved obligation.
Costs: depends on a fact about the escalation module the context states from memory: that the obligation is recomputed, not consumed on dispatch.
Forces: the trace text carries an instruction ('send another turn to get the ruling'), which is prose the human has to notice.

options.text: The failure writes a pending item the human retries from the queue, which re-dispatches the same turn.
pcr: Buys: the obligation is a thing on the board with a button, not an instruction in a notice.
Costs: a pending-queue kind for a re-dispatch, and the lane has to be able to replay a turn it has already recorded as accepted.
Forces: the spec's node-scoped retry and this queue retry become two retry mechanisms unless one is built on the other.

options.text: Hand the channel up to the expert on failure, on the theory that a killed first-rung seat is the escalation module's fourth condition (a seat lacking an input) read off a transport fact.
pcr: Buys: the next turn runs on the seat most likely to answer.
Costs: the seat that died in the last session was already the expert; handing up from it goes nowhere.
Forces: a new escalation condition read off the lane rather than off the human's turn or the seat's reply, which the module's founding rule may or may not admit.

decisions.title: What does a retry of a killed CLI turn actually resume?
decisions.body: Both expert transports are resumed single-process chains, and a turn killed on the timeout was a subprocess killed mid-answer. Whether the CLI's own session file recorded the killed turn decides whether a retry re-sends the prompt or resumes a half-written answer. The context does not state what either CLI does when killed.

options.text: Treat a killed turn as never sent: the retry re-sends the same prompt on the same resumed chain, and the transcript copy taken after the retry is the record.
pcr: Buys: one code path for retry; no reading of the CLI's session file.
Costs: if the CLI did record the killed turn, the chain now holds the prompt twice and the model sees its own aborted answer.
Forces: whoever implements this has to establish what 'claude -p --resume' and 'codex exec resume' do with a turn whose process was killed, from the CLIs' own behaviour, not from memory.

options.text: Before a retry, read the transcript copy taken after the last completed turn and start a fresh chain from it if the CLI's session file has moved past it.
pcr: Buys: the model never sees an aborted answer as its own prior turn.
Costs: a comparison between the session directory's transcript copy and the CLI's live session file, whose formats differ per CLI.
Forces: the transcript copy becomes load-bearing for correctness, not just for the record.

options.text: No retry mechanism in this slice: the trace tells the human, and the human's next turn is the retry, whatever the chain holds.
pcr: Buys: the smallest slice; nothing about CLI session semantics is decided here.
Costs: the open question about killed turns is deferred to whoever next sees a doubled prompt in a transcript.
Forces: d2(a) or nothing; d2(b) needs a retry to exist.

mootness.answer: Render the existing error-phase status entry as a notice in the notification lane, homed on the channel, with the tier and the reason in its text.
